text:
maria: Hi all — first week here! Quick question about API keys and sandbox: I have a hosted API key in the console, but when I try to run a streaming request from my laptop behind the company proxy it fails with a connection reset. Is there a recommended way to run streaming locally or should I use the sandbox?

sruthi: welcome, maria :tada:  For most quick experiments use the sandbox key — it has relaxed quotas and is safe for toy data. Hosted keys are for prod/dev envs and may be routed through our gateway requiring specific proxy allowlist.

jamie: pinging infra: if you're behind corp proxy, you need to set HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY env vars and also add our gateway CA to your trust store if you see TLS errors. Streaming should work if proxy allows websockets or long polling.

maria: thanks — I get a 502 on streaming specifically. non-streaming REST calls succeed with the hosted key.

alex: 502 on streaming usually means the proxy is closing the connection. Two options: 1) run from a laptop on an open network (home), 2) use the sandbox endpoint which supports chunked responses over plain HTTPS (less sensitive to proxy ws support).

sruthi: note on quotas: sandbox has its own quota bucket (low by default), hosted keys have token-based billing and different rate limits per team tier. If you hit 429, we return a Retry-After header. Backoff is recommended.

maria: curious — where do I check my sandbox quota and request more?

sruthi: check Console > Usage > Sandbox Quotas (or the quick link in the onboarding doc). To request more, open a ticket in #help or DM me and I can escalate. Typical turnaround is same day for small bumps.

jamie: quick commands that help debug:
```
# test non-streaming
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate
\n# streaming (ws) test (if you have wscat)
wscat -c wss://stream.api.redwood.dev/v1/stream -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY"
```

alex: if you must use hosted key behind proxy and streaming is required, we often spin a small bastion in the dev VPC and tunnel requests through it. That's heavier though.

maria: ok — I'll try sandbox for now and file a ticket if I need more quota. One last thing: are there any local env var names or config patterns we use so my code is ready for switch to hosted?

sruthi: yes — use REDWOOD_API_KEY for runtime, REDWOOD_API_URL for endpoint override (points to sandbox by default for new accounts). Keep key out of source, use secrets manager for prod. Also add graceful handling for 429 and 5xx (retries with exponential backoff).

onboarding-bot: reminder: onboarding checklist step 4 incomplete — link to Console and API key rotation guide sent to your DMs.

maria: perfect, thanks everyone! saving the commands and will escalate if quota blocks me. :pray:
